successCriteria.description: The LeaveBalance entity exposes exactly the canonical fields (id, employeeId, policyId, totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays, fiscalYear, status, createdAt, updatedAt) with status constrained to 'ACTIVE' | 'CLOSED' | 'FORECAST', and imports Employee and LeavePolicy types from their respective module entry points for reference typing.
The ILeaveBalanceRepository interface declares all seven operations: findById, findByEmployeeId, findByEmployeeAndPolicy, findByEmployeeAndFiscalYear, save, update, and incrementUsedDays.
PgLeaveBalanceRepository implements ILeaveBalanceRepository and performs all database access exclusively through the shared pool in src/shared/db/connection.ts (no inline SQL outside the repository).

incrementUsedDays performs an atomic increment of used_days (supporting positive and negative deltas) and returns the updated balance row, satisfying the materialized balance rule that deductions/restorations happen transactionally.

Jest unit tests in tests/unit/modules/leave-balance/ cover the model field shape and every repository method (including the not-found/null paths and the atomic increment path), with the shared db pool mocked.

constraints: No use of `any` — use `unknown` with type guards instead (HARNESS.json no-any rule, severity high).

All database access must go through the repository pattern via the shared pool in src/shared/db/connection.ts; no direct DB calls outside the repository (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository, critical).

Modules import from each other ONLY through their declared public entry point (index.ts); leave-balance must import Employee and LeavePolicy types via the employee and leave-policy module index files, not from internal model files (AGENTS.md architecture rule 1).
Strict TypeScript must pass (no implicit any, strict null checks) — the phase must compile under tsc --noEmit and pass the Jest unit suite.
No circular dependencies: leave-balance depends on employee and leave-policy, which must not import back from leave-balance (AGENTS.md architecture rule 1 / reconciled dependency map).
outOfScope: LeaveBalance service (ILeaveBalanceService / LeaveBalanceService) — deferred to Phase 8.
LeaveBalance controller and Fastify routes — balance is read/written internally by the LeaveRequest service in later phases; no HTTP surface this phase.
Database migrations / DDL for the leave_balances table — this phase creates the model and repository only, not the schema migration.
Balance initialization logic, sufficiency checks, and business-day counting — these are service-layer concerns (Phase 8 / Phase 9), not repository concerns.
Audit logging for balance mutations (GP-002) — audit module does not exist yet (Phase 10); the repository layer itself does not emit audit records.

ambiguities.description: The binding business rule states remaining_days = total_entitlement - used_days is "computed, not stored", yet the canonical LeaveBalance entity includes remainingDays as a field and the reconciled SQL schema lists remaining_days as a stored column. It is ambiguous whether the repository must persist remaining_days or recompute it on read/write.
options: Store remaining_days as a column and keep it in sync (remaining = total - used) on every write, including incrementUsedDays
Treat remainingDays as a computed/transient field not persisted to the table, derived from totalEntitlement - usedDays at map time

ambiguities.description: incrementUsedDays must not allow used_days to exceed total_entitlement, but it is unspecified whether the repository enforces this guard itself (rejecting the increment) or whether enforcement is deferred to the service layer (Phase 8/9).
options: Repository enforces the guard: incrementUsedDays rejects/clamps when used_days + delta > total_entitlement
Repository performs a pure atomic increment without guard; the service layer validates sufficiency before calling

ambiguities.description: The phase scope says to "import Employee and LeavePolicy types from their respective modules for reference typing" but does not specify whether these imports are used only as type-only imports (import type) for documentation/FK typing, or whether the repository performs existence checks against the employee/policy repositories at save time.
options: Type-only imports for FK reference typing; no cross-repository existence checks in the repository layer
Repository validates employeeId/policyId existence by querying employee and leave-policy repositories before save

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeaveBalance row is unique per (employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear) combination — there is at most one balance row per employee per policy per fiscal year (reconciled schema unique constraint on employee_id + policy_id + fiscal_year).

remainingDays must equal totalEntitlement minus usedDays at all times — remaining_days is a computed/materialized value of total_entitlement - used_days, never independently set to an arbitrary value (binding business rule: materialized transactional balance).
status is constrained to the lifecycle states ACTIVE, CLOSED, or FORECAST; only ACTIVE balances are drawable, CLOSED are historical, FORECAST are future-year balances not yet usable.
usedDays must never exceed totalEntitlement (an employee cannot consume more leave than entitled) — the atomic increment must not drive used_days above total_entitlement.
employeeId references an existing Employee and policyId references an existing LeavePolicy (foreign keys to employees.id and leave_policies.id per the reconciled conceptual data model).

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns the matching LeaveBalance or null when no row exists; never throws on not-found.
Returns an array (possibly empty) of all LeaveBalance rows for the employee; never null.
Returns the matching LeaveBalance or null; resolves the unique (employee, policy) lookup.
Returns an array (possibly empty) of LeaveBalance rows for the employee in the given fiscal year.
Persists a new LeaveBalance row and returns the persisted entity; a duplicate (employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear) must be rejected rather than silently overwriting.
Applies a partial update to the existing balance, refreshes updatedAt, and returns the updated entity or null when the id does not exist.

Atomically increments used_days by the given delta (positive for deduction, negative for restoration) within a single statement, recomputes remaining_days = total_entitlement - used_days, and returns the updated balance or null when the id does not exist; must not allow used_days to exceed total_entitlement.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The LeaveBalance entity shape must match the reconciled canonical attributes exactly (id, employeeId, policyId, totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays, fiscalYear, status, createdAt, updatedAt) and the status union ('ACTIVE' | 'CLOSED' | 'FORECAST') — do not add, rename, or omit fields.

The Employee type must be imported via the employee module's public entry point (index.ts), matching how leave-policy imports LeaveType from shared-types — never import directly from employee.model.ts.
The LeavePolicy type must be imported via the leave-policy module's public entry point (index.ts), consistent with the module-boundary rule that cross-module imports go through index.ts only.

PgLeaveBalanceRepository must obtain its database connection from the shared pool exported by src/shared/db/connection.ts, matching the pattern established by PgEmployeeRepository and PgLeavePolicyRepository.

The repository must follow the established repository pattern: an interface (ILeaveBalanceRepository) paired with a Pg* implementation class, a private mapRow helper converting snake_case DB columns to camelCase entity fields, and update returning null on missing id — matching PgEmployeeRepository and PgLeavePolicyRepository conventions.

Unit tests must mock the shared db pool via jest.mock('shared/db/connection') and assert both the returned entity mapping and the SQL/parameters passed to pool.query, matching the test conventions in the employee and leave-policy repository test files.

integrationPoints.why: LeaveBalance.employeeId references Employee; the model imports the Employee type for reference typing and the repository's foreign-key semantics depend on employees.id existing.
LeaveBalance.policyId references LeavePolicy; the model imports the LeavePolicy type for reference typing and the repository's foreign-key semantics depend on leave_policies.id existing.
PgLeaveBalanceRepository executes SQL against PostgreSQL through the shared pool, the single permitted database access point.

The LeaveRequest service will consume ILeaveBalanceRepository.incrementUsedDays to atomically deduct and restore balance on approval/rejection/cancellation — this repository's atomic increment contract is the integration seam for the materialized balance rule.

The future LeaveBalanceService will inject ILeaveBalanceRepository to implement getBalance, initializeBalance, getRemainingDays, and hasSufficientBalance — the repository interface defined this phase is the service's dependency seam.
